title: Programmable microdevices: real connections and selective local rework
status_authority: Whole supplied source at its stated assumptions and read scopes; no Capital science execution, physical qualification or new independent audit.
reported_status: ROOT credits actual magnetic/capillary part assembly and maker-configurable circuits, then derives introduced coupled electrical/thermal rework cases. Low electrical resistance can heat neighboring parts during release and later cooldown, but a higher-resistance alternative can pass the introduced temperature limit without a new isolator. A proposed thermal disconnect requires real contacts, retention, access and restoration. No useful heterogeneous 3D device, selective-rework apparatus, novel algorithm, qualified material or whole-operation advantage is established.

Actual part geometry, electrical function, mechanical retention, joining, neighboring heat, failed-part extraction, reconnecting and finite stock renewal belong to the useful assembly/rework operation. The thermal model assumes four constant-resistance diffusive metal-like bridges with Lorenz-law electronic heat flux, two lumped enthalpy/thermal nodes and an introduced melt fraction release criterion; other heat paths are not automatically removed.

The Lorenz model is not universal to real contacts; actual substrate, fluid, radiation and mechanical heat paths remain. Complete release/rejoin and useful device function are unconstructed. Numerical energy residuals and timestep checks validate only the declared calculation, not materials. No novel device, universal obstruction or advantage is claimed.
